key_insight: A multitask neural network can jointly predict UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness well, but stacking ensemble learning gives more accurate task-specific predictions overall.
engineering_relevance: This comparison helps welding engineers choose between shared-learning models for efficiency and ensemble models for highest predictive precision in process optimization and quality control.
method: Train a multitask neural network with shared hidden layers and task-specific outputs.
Train a stacking ensemble on the same welding dataset for separate outputs.
Compare both models using RMSE and R² across UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports MTNN RMSE/R² of 0.1288/0.6724 for UTS, 0.0886/0.9215 for weld hardness, and 0.1125/0.8407 for HAZ hardness, while stacking achieved 0.0263/0.9863, 0.0467/0.9782, and 0.1109/0.8453, respectively.
watch_item: Stacking performs best here, but it may require more tuning and may not generalize as efficiently as multitask learning when data are sparse or tasks are more strongly coupled.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
